title: Region affinity orchestration: latency and network-health-driven routing
creator: Ana Patel
description: Build a production-safe routing decision service that combines rolling p50/p95 latency telemetry with a composite network health score (latency, packet loss, error rate, jitter) to drive region selection and model-variant fallback. The goal is to reduce latency SLO violations and improve overall availability by automatically preferring regions with better observed end-to-end performance while gracefully degrading to compatible model variants when capacity or network conditions warrant it. This ticket covers the scoring algorithm, smoothing/decay rules, per-customer affinity overrides, API surface, and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Routing service exposes /decide endpoint returning preferred region and model_variant with reason-code and score breakdown
Decisions use rolling windowed p50 and p95 and network health score computed from telemetry (prometheus + ingest service)
Default policy: prefer region with best weighted_score (0.6*p95_norm + 0.3*p50_norm + 0.1*nethealth_penalty) — configurable via runtime flags
Graceful fallback: if chosen region's p95 & nethealth indicate degraded state, return a compatible model_variant (quantized/fast) instead of higher-latency variant
Canary rollout limited to 5% of traffic for 48 hours with automated rollback on >2x baseline error-rate or >15% increase in latency p95
Dashboard shows per-region decisions, percent traffic steered, and a histogram of p50/p95 windows used for decisions
Unit and integration tests cover scoring, TTL/decay, and deterministic tie-breaking logic
implementation_notes: Telemetry input: use the existing metrics pipeline (edge-exporter -> prometheus/ingest) to feed a mini aggregations job that emits per-region rolling summaries every 10s
Windowing: 1-min sliding window for p50, 5-min decayed window for p95 (exponential decay alpha=0.25) to balance responsiveness and stability
Outlier handling: clip p95 above 5s as 'network outage' sentinel and apply aggressive penalty to nethealth score
Network health score components: packet_loss (0-1), error_rate (0-1), jitter_ms normalized to 0-1. Combine as nethealth_penalty = min(1, 0.5*packet_loss + 0.4*error_rate + 0.1*(jitter_ms/200))
Normalization: p50_norm and p95_norm scale to [0,1] relative to target SLOs (p50_target=50ms, p95_target=200ms), values >1 clamp to 1
Decision TTL: caching decisions per user (or token) for 15s to avoid flapping; allow override for low-latency-required routes
Priority overrides: enterprise customers can pin region or disable automatic routing; respect RBAC and audit logs
Model variant matching: use tag compatibility list (e.g., [gptx-1.0, gptx-1.0-quant]) stored in catalog service to select the closest model variant
Safety: fall back to cross-region synchronous routing only if local region unreachable for >30s; otherwise prefer variant fallback to maintain latency SLO
Config: expose weights and thresholds via feature flags (console + remote config) for iterative tuning
rollout_plan: Phase 0: deploy scoring service behind feature flag; no traffic steering (read-only) for 1 week to validate signals
Phase 1: enable canary steering at 1% traffic for 24h, monitor errors/latency; abort on >2x error-rate or >20% p95 increase
Phase 2: expand to 5% for 48h with synthetic workload tests and manual review
Phase 3: 25% with adaptive dampening enabled (increase decay factor to prevent oscillation), run for 72h
Phase 4: full rollout with 7-day observation window and automated rollback triggers configured in runbook
testing_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and normalization edge cases
Integration tests simulating multi-region telemetry with controlled packet loss and spikes
Chaos experiments: inject high jitter in primary region and assert fallback variant selection without global outage
Load tests: verify decision API latency <5ms at 10k qps with caching enabled
User-level AB test to measure perceived latency and error-rate for real traffic buckets
monitoring_slo_targets: Regional steer success rate >= 99.5% (requests that reached selected region without additional reroute)
Total product p95 latency improved or unchanged for 95% of customers during canary
No more than 0.5% increase in global error-rate during rollout
